grammar_errors.mistake: Date: he stopped at ألفين (2000) and dropped ستة وعشرين; she supplied the full year ألفين ستة وعشرين; she also confirmed day-first order عشرة تسعة at 06:46.
grammar_errors.fix: I just did it. I just repeated what you said. ألفين ستة وعشرين.

grammar_errors.mistake: Clock time: he said talaat (three, masc/short form) for the time; she asked three or two, he fixed to intayn and she recast الساعة تنتين إلا تلت (feminine number after el-saa3a).
grammar_errors.said: Sa alaat ila nun-- ila tult.

grammar_errors.mistake: Answering her كيف الجو عندكم اليوم he said جو كتير كتير: 'the weather' is a known thing and takes el- (her prompt and the sheet row 'it's hot | El-jaw shoab | الجو شوب' both have الجو). The adjective شوب is absent in the transcript but she answered عن جد؟ as if she heard a complete statement, so the missing word is likely an ASR drop and is not scored - only the el- is. B reading.
'A video on YouTube' takes على, he used لـ (for/of); she let it pass; YouTube itself is not on her sheet so the English word is not an error.
Profession idafa: the second noun takes el- (مهندس الكهربا); he left it bare and she recast.
grammar_errors.said: مهندس-- Do you guys say مهندس كهرباء؟

grammar_errors.mistake: Saying who the man he called is - 'he is not a kahrabji, he is an engineer' - is a present noun predicate: Levantine negates it with مش and no 'to be' (C4); ما يكون is neither that nor a licensed ykoon context (B8: only after lamma/iza or for habits). The man's job is a present fact, so ما كان (r2) is not the target either. She said nothing about it; her 10:30 صلح لي moves to his next clause.
grammar_errors.said: ما، ما يكون، uh, كهربج-- uh, كهربجي، هو مهندس، uh, مهندس.

grammar_errors.mistake: 'For me' rides on the preposition (لي), not as an object ending on the verb (صلحني = he fixed me, 10:44); she separated the two forms.
Masculine colour adjective after the feminine noun بلوزة; her recast is transcribed as بدائية (almost certainly وردية) and she said صح when he repeated the feminine form at 12:14.
He said 'stayed my house' with no preposition; she prompted 'bi or fi?' and he fixed to بي بيتي at 12:50.
grammar_errors.said: اه، this is take Allah بيتي.

grammar_errors.mistake: Explaining why he stayed home today (اليوم ضليت بي بيتي): 'because there is AC' - existence in the plain present is في / عندي, not يكون (B8: ykoon only after lamma/iza or for habits; C1: no 'to be' in the present). She moved on to شو بتتذكر at 13:04 without a fix. 'air conditioning' is not on her sheet, so the English word itself is not an error. B reading.

'One word': the modifier وحدة sits after the noun like an adjective; he put it first (English order) and she recast noun-first, بس كلمة وحدة. A7 is the rule broken (modifier after the noun); E1 is the secondary tag because the modifier is the number one.

'Two verbs' takes the dual فعلين, not فعل + تنين (E1: 2 has its own form). Her reply mirrors his phrase (أههم بس فعل-) and 'فعلاً' ('indeed') makes no sense after أههم بس, so it is almost certainly فعلين mis-transcribed - filed as her recast. Medium because the transcript does not show the ين.
grammar_errors.said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،

grammar_errors.mistake: 'I annoyed you' said with an extra -ti- (زعجتيك, the you-f ending) instead of I-past زعجتك; Amal recast زعجتك or أزعجتك. His أزعشتك at 15:02 is S4.

Drill 'you got annoyed with me': after انزعجتي he started ما (reaching for 'with me'); she asked ليش ما؟, he answered 'You said with by me... مني، مني sorry' (16:10) and gave انزعجتي مني at 16:22 ('Perfect'). انزعج takes من (her 14:35: 'annoyed with you you would say مِنْ'). Medium: his ما may partly be a stutter of ماضي, but her question and his fix show she heard a wrong preposition.
Masculine participle for a female addressee; she asked 'inti or inta?' and he fixed to مزعوجة at 18:54.
'he' form verb for plural 'many things'
grammar_errors.fix: بزعجوني. بزعجوني. ... you could say بتزعجني بس مش بزعجني.

grammar_errors.mistake: Plural subject 'many things' needs the plural verb بزعجوني; he used the singular; she recast twice and he acknowledged 'it's plural'.
grammar_errors.said: And then باز is not بازوج, بازيجيني هدول اليوم.

grammar_errors.mistake: Same plural-agreement slip repeated on his second attempt; she recast بزعجوني and he fixed at 20:33.
'These days' needs the plural أيام; he used the singular اليوم and she recast.
The noun after هدول keeps its el-; he dropped it in the fixed version and she moved on (طيب).
grammar_errors.said: أيام. I even wrote أيام. هدول أيام.

grammar_errors.mistake: 'Are you sure THAT you didn't annoy him' needs إنو; he used اللي. She asked 'why illi?' (21:27) and said إنو مش اللي.
'you (pl) didn't annoy HIM' is missing the object ending -ه on the verb; she moved to the illi problem and let this pass.
After إذا ما she keeps the b- (إذا ما بشوف); he used the bare أشوفك; he repeated her form at 22:31. Her ruling here differs from the plain B3 drop, so filed under B3 as her exception.
grammar_errors.fix: بس مبسوطة إذا ما بشوف هيك.

grammar_errors.mistake: Negative command: he gave the positive imperative إنزعجي for 'don't be annoyed'; she prompted 'so don't be', he produced ما تنزعج (23:24) then ما تنزعجي (23:32) after her echo.
kept b- after 'it wasn't their intention to'
After مش قصدهم ('they didn't mean to') the verb drops its b-: يدايقوكي; he kept the b- and insisted 'أنا بعرف هيك' at 25:16. Pronouncing دايق as تاي is S4, not counted.
Idafa: the first word never takes el- (أول الفعل / أول الكلمة); he put el- on both. She let it pass.
grammar_errors.said: الـ أول الـ فعل، الـ أول الكلمة.

grammar_errors.mistake: 3pl past needs -u (كسروا); he gave كسرت; her echo prompted him and he fixed at 28:47, confirmed 28:53.
In the present-tense drill (هم ...) he dropped the b-: يكسروا for بيكسروا; she let it pass.

'You keep breaking my plates': after إنتِ بتظلي the verb needs the you-f prefix بت- (بتكسري). His production is transcribed only as the tail زري and she said she did not hear the t, i.e. the person marker was missing; he fixed to بتكسري at 33:31. Low: the transcript holds only a fragment, so whether he said بكسري (B18) or كسري (B1) cannot be shown.

Asked for the past (ماضي, 36:38) of the in-verb بنكسر he offered a form ASR wrote as 'Next far' (most likely نكسر without the initial alef); Amal recast the past as انكسر (with the 'in-' onset) and he repeated انكسر at 37:05; low because his exact form is unrecoverable from the transcript.
grammar_errors.said: Next far. Is it next far?
grammar_errors.fix: So it's either inكسر or انكسر.

grammar_errors.mistake: MSA 2pl past ending -تم instead of Levantine -توا; she let it pass in the conjugation run.
el- on a noun that has a possessive ending
'His cups' needs the plural كاسات + ه; he used the singular كاسته; she recast كساته.

For 'his cup' she recast كاسه; his كاسته keeps the -t- of كاسة before the possessive (sheet has 'cup | Kaasa | كاسة'), which is normally fine, so low - the transcript may have dropped her vowel (كاستو).
كاسة is feminine so the verb is انكسرت; he used the masculine; she recast and confirmed 'because it's female' at 41:00.
made كان feminine to match 'she' instead of عمر
grammar_errors.said: or كان عمرها أو عمرها كان؟ كانت. ... كانت، right؟
grammar_errors.fix: Both، بس كان عمر is better. كان عمرها. ... لأ، كان عمرها صح.

grammar_errors.mistake: The subject is عمر (masc), so كان, not كانت, even though it is 'her' age; he pushed for كانت twice (43:36, 43:43) and she said لأ.

Conjugating انكسر for هو/هي he produced بينكسري (masc بي- prefix + fem -ي ending), a form that exists for no subject; she did not fix it, she redirected him to the skipped إنتو. Low: he was switching subjects mid-word. Her هو at 45:38 fixes a different slip (هي بينكسر).
He gave the he-form بينكسر for هي; she said هو (that form is for he); he then produced هي بتنكسر (45:46) and she said حلو.
grammar_errors.said: Uh, هي بينكسو-- بينكسر. هو بينكسر.

grammar_errors.mistake: إحنا of the un-verb انكسر is بننكسر (b-n-nkasir); he gave بنكسر, which is the إحنا form of plain كسر ('we break'), and she went straight into usage talk (46:08). Low: ASR may have collapsed the double ن, and her 45:57 line (transcribed بتنكسر) may itself have been her feeding him بننكسر.
'I never broke anything' is past; he used present because he thought أبداً forces present; she asked بكسر أو كسرت, he fixed to ما كسرت (52:36) and she confirmed كسرت.
Negate the verb with ما (ما نمت منيح), not مش before the adverb; she recast and he repeated at 53:54.
made a regular -aat plural of فعل instead of the broken plural
Naming the verb pair he gave the bare أكسر; she recast بكسر and بنكسر.
grammar_errors.said: is it بزور بنكسر؟ بنكسر. أكسر. Okay.
